intro: Section 34.4 surveys the theories of personality and psychopathology that grew out of psychoanalysis. Its first part, built here, follows Sigmund Freud from his neurologic training and the case of Anna O to his early models of the mind. You will meet the dream theory of 1900, the topographic model of conscious, preconscious and unconscious, the drive theory with its libido, aggression and life and death instincts, infantile sexuality and narcissism, and the psychosexual stages from oral to genital. Everything here is Freud's theory as the chapter reports it, with the later critiques the chapter itself notes; update boxes add historical corrections.
objectives: Outline Freud's early career, the collaboration with Breuer and what the case of Anna O taught him, including how the treatment ended.
Define manifest and latent content, the censor and day residue, and explain condensation, displacement, symbolic representation and secondary revision.
Compare the conscious, preconscious and unconscious systems, describe primary process thinking, and state why Freud gave up the topographic model.
Describe the source, impetus, aim and object of an instinct, the changes in Freud's drive theory from 1905 to 1923, and the pleasure and reality principles.
Explain Freud's ideas on infantile sexuality, object relationships and narcissism, and note which of them later research or practice has questioned.
For each psychosexual stage, give the approximate ages, the focus, the objectives and the pathologic and healthy character traits the chapter lists.
